title: The Li River's ¥20-Note Fisherman Quit in 2008 | China Travel Expert
description:
The cormorant fisherman on the back of China's ¥20 note? The famous ones quit fishing in 2008 — and now they pose for photographers.

The banknote view is the Li River at Xingping, below Yellow Cloth Shoal. Its most photographed fishermen, the Huang brothers, gave up catching fish for a living around 2008 and work as professional models; the cormorant "fishing" you snap at dawn is largely a performance. Overfishing and ecology made posing for cameras pay far better than the river ever did. The birds are real — the fishing scene is mostly for show.

🧭 Expert Tip: For the real banknote view, go to Xingping's Yellow Cloth Shoal (漓江兴坪) — that bend of the Li River is the ¥20-note scene, with or without a fisherman.

漓江¥20纸币上的鸬鹚渔翁，早已不靠打鱼为生——摆拍比捕鱼更挣钱。
